why: I built my own 16 pairs from a paper I chose myself (arXiv 2611.00401, physics.chem-ph, VESPER free-energy estimation), wrote my own surface criterion at T3, then wrote my own expected answers at T4 by applying a mapping I had registered at T0. Running the frozen criterion over the blind pairs gives 13/16 = 0.8125 agreement with those answers. That sits in the pre-registered PARTIAL band 0.60 <= agreement < 0.90, with the purity admission passed, so the tree lands on EXTERNAL_PARTIAL and nothing else. The three disagreements are not scattered: they are exactly the three pairs where a quantity was rewritten in a smaller unit of the same dimension (10 ns vs 10000 ps, 25 ns vs 25000 ps, 100 ns vs 100000 ps). My criterion compares stated values only, so it sees the numeral disappear and rejects; my registered fact mapping says the asserted quantity survived, so it accepts. Both readings are internally consistent - the surface string genuinely does not re-state the numeral, and the physics genuinely does not change - which is precisely the interpretive latitude this tier exists to record rather than to smooth over. I did not add unit-prefix arithmetic to the criterion to close the gap: that would have been tuning after the fact, which the brief forbids (section 7 discipline 6), and criterion_note.md section 3 records the rejected alternative in advance.

metrics.mismatch_explanation: dimensionally equal re-expression of one quantity; criterion is numeral-based, registered fact is quantity-based

purity_admission.preregistered_findings: no import of any kind, no open/eval/exec, no os/sys/random/time/datetime/pathlib attribute, no label-field identifier, no hardcoded pair id; repeated runs and order-reversed runs give identical output

what_this_does_and_does_not_claim.claims: An independently chosen corpus, an independently built sample set, an independently induced surface criterion and an independently registered truth mapping reproduce the *shape* of the transferability finding: a purely surface-inducted deterministic rule tracks the objective textual facts on most but not all construction families, and where it fails it fails systematically on one identifiable family rather than randomly.
what_this_does_and_does_not_claim.does_not_claim: It does not confirm or refute the委托方's own verdict. I never read their criterion, samples, knowledge base, or any historical adjudication, and I have no idea whether their rule sees unit prefixes. Agreement or disagreement between our two verdicts is a mechanical comparison the委托方 must perform on their side; pre-empting it here would destroy the independence this delivery is supposed to provide.
limits: n=16 from one single-domain paper; the O_PERMUTE and O_HEDGE_SWAP families could not be instantiated at all on the mechanically selected sentences, so two registered families are untested rather than passed

the pool-selection rule (every third number-bearing sentence) pulled in two structural fragments rather than measurement sentences - P01 is the table of contents and P06 is a proof-environment heading - where the numerals are section labels, not quantities; my criterion treats them like any other numeral, which is defensible for a surface rule but weakens what those two pairs demonstrate

I am the author of both sides of the ledger, so 'independent' here means independent of the委托方, not independent of myself; the mitigations and their residual risk are stated in criterion_note.md section 4
the criterion's rejections are only as good as the claim that every numeral in a scientific sentence is a stated quantity; reference years and figure numbers ride along
